title: gRPC versus REST (when to choose each for APIs)
hook: Representational State Transfer (REST) with JSON over Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is the default for public Web APIs. gRPC uses Protocol Buffers (protobuf) over HTTP/2 for fast, strongly typed communication — ideal for internal service-to-service calls but awkward for browser clients.

blocks.text: REST APIs expose resources as URLs with JSON bodies — human-readable, cacheable, works everywhere including browsers and GitHub Pages static clients. gRPC defines services and messages in a .proto file, generates C# client and server stubs, and sends compact binary protobuf over HTTP/2 with built-in streaming (server, client, bidirectional). ASP.NET Core supports both: MapControllers for REST, MapGrpcService for gRPC. Choose based on caller type, performance needs, and whether you need browser support.

entries.plainDefinition: High-performance RPC framework using protobuf serialization and HTTP/2 transport.
Binary serialization format defined in .proto schema files — smaller and faster than JSON.
entries.example: message OrderReply { string id = 1; string status = 2; }

entries.plainDefinition: Multiplexed protocol enabling multiple streams over one connection — required by gRPC.
entries.example: gRPC requires HTTP/2; REST typically uses HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2

entries.plainDefinition: Proxy layer allowing browser clients to call gRPC via HTTP/1.1 — adds complexity.
entries.example: Envoy proxy translates grpc-web to gRPC

blocks.text: Microservices behind a gateway often use gRPC internally for low latency and strong contracts, while the public API remains REST/JSON for mobile apps and third parties. Wrong choice costs money: JSON REST for high-volume internal fan-out adds CPU and bandwidth; gRPC for a public API blocked by corporate proxies causes integration pain. This is a standard senior system design question on Reddit r/dotnet and LeetCode.

blocks.title: Hybrid pattern
blocks.body: Public: REST + OpenAPI. Internal east-west: gRPC between services. BFF aggregates gRPC backends, exposes REST to clients. Same domain logic, two presentation protocols.

snippet.explanation: Clean Architecture shines here — Application handler shared, REST and gRPC are thin adapters. Measure payload and latency in staging before choosing public gRPC.

blocks.title: gRPC vs REST across stacks
rows: REST native; gRPC needs grpc-web proxy

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: gRPC for public browser-facing API without grpc-web proxy. Exposing gRPC without TLS in production. Breaking proto field numbers on deploy — use field reservation. Using gRPC through HTTP/1.1-only load balancers. Duplicating business logic in REST controller and gRPC service instead of shared Application layer.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: Application Insights dependency tracking shows gRPC call duration vs REST for same operation. Load test internal fan-out: 1000 calls/sec REST JSON vs gRPC — compare CPU and p99. Network: protobuf ~60% smaller payloads. Operational: grpc-health-probe for K8s gRPC health checks (different from HTTP /health). Versioning: add new rpc methods, never reuse field numbers, use package versioning. When interviewer asks 'why not GraphQL' — GraphQL is client-driven query aggregation; gRPC is service contract RPC.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying gRPC replaces REST everywhere. Not knowing browsers cannot call gRPC natively. Unable to explain protobuf contract versioning. Claiming REST is always slower without acknowledging HTTP/2 REST exists. No mention of BFF pattern for hybrid architectures.

interviewTakeaways: REST/JSON for public and browser APIs; gRPC/protobuf for internal service-to-service performance.
gRPC requires HTTP/2 — blocked by some proxies; browsers need grpc-web proxy layer.
Production tip: shared Application handlers behind REST and gRPC adapters; grpc-health-probe in K8s.
60s: Public REST OpenAPI. Internal gRPC for low latency binary RPC. Proto defines contract. Cannot call gRPC from browser natively. BFF exposes REST, calls gRPC backends. Version proto carefully.
Follow-up: how do you handle gRPC load balancing and health checks in Kubernetes?
commonPitfalls: gRPC for public browser API gets you rejected — no native browser support without grpc-web.
Duplicating business logic in REST and gRPC instead of shared Application layer.

Strong answer: 'REST public third-party and mobile JSON. gRPC internal east-west HTTP/2 protobuf. BFF pattern. Shared MediatR handlers. grpcurl for debug. Measure p99 and payload size. grpc-web only if browser must call gRPC directly.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: NestJS @nestjs/microservices supports gRPC transport with proto files — same internal vs external split. Public REST controller, internal gRPC microservice communication.
Node microservices use @grpc/grpc-js for internal RPC and Express for public REST — identical hybrid pattern. grpc-web requires Envoy or similar proxy for browser clients.
